rejected_structural_assertions: Payment must be outbound and settle this vendor invoice
Purchase order, receipt and invoice line links differ
Receipt not linked to purchase order
requirements: One vendor, one vendor location, one purchased and stocked product and one product-price record.
One purchase order, one receipt and one vendor invoice, each with exactly one product line.
Receipt line links to purchase-order line; invoice line links to receipt line. Example: PO line A -> receipt line B -> invoice line C referencing B.
All purchasing headers use the same vendor/location, sales flag false; one outbound payment settles that vendor invoice.
Native receipt creates one inbound inventory movement. Matching and costing rows must belong to this document chain, client, organization, product and accounting schema.
Allocation headers are completed; invoice/payment/allocation postings exist and balance. Posting guard does not prevent internal costing or reposting.
Explicit posting must use JourneySupport.postOnce. Direct postDocument, postImmediate, document-factory access and reflective posting dispatch are forbidden, including force/repost variants.

Trace numbers use BigDecimal or integer values; Float/Double are forbidden. SQL-NULL is reserved for actual null. Ordinary duplicate keys are rejected; only declared lifecycle fields may be explicitly replaced.
Accounting schemas are read-only except native MPeriod period-cache updates (C_Period_ID, Updated, UpdatedBy) tied to the journey postings. Accounting configuration edits are forbidden.

Every delta in M_MatchInv, M_MatchPO, M_CostDetail, M_Product_PO, M_CostQueue, M_CostHistory and T_Fact_Acct_History must belong to the journey client, organization, product, vendor and document chain. Other products and pre-existing costing/history rows must remain unchanged.
Existing owned M_Product_PO rows may update only PriceLastPO, PriceLastInv, PriceEffective, Updated and UpdatedBy; deletion or any other update is rejected.

For this declared one-line journey, accounting history permits at most four rows and at most one row per document/schema/currency/account combination, derived from the deterministic reference. This is a bounded structural rule, not general costing qualification.
selector_semantics: Each only(table, conditions) requires exactly one matching committed row; stages declared in the base public contract must each identify exactly one row.
